item.text: {"text":"I found no verified GRU4Rec study reporting the exact three-way comparison: suffix cropping, full-context training with the identical retained-target mask, and matched supervised-target budgets. Closest evidence: [Petrov and Macdonald’s Recency Sampling](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/273792/2/273792.pdf) explicitly studies target selection, including GRU4Rec; samples a sequence-length-dependent number of targets with recency weighting and compares training objectives/losses. It changes supervision and input construction together, so it does not establish an isolated historical-context effect. [CL4SRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.14395) uses cropping to construct auxiliary contrastive views alongside next-item prediction; its augmentation comparison addresses a different question from cropping every-position supervised GRU training.\n\nFor the proposed experiment, the necessary control follows from the objective: compare cropped inputs against full inputs with losses enabled at exactly the same original target positions, identical negatives, and identical loss denominators. Reset the cropped GRU state at the crop boundary; preserve the full prefix in the masked full-context arm. This isolates access to earlier history for retained predictions. Add full-context/all-target training to quantify the effect of discarded supervision. Specify token averaging, Σmℓ/Σm, versus averaging each sequence’s mean loss: these assign different relative weights to long and short histories. Dividing by padded B×L additionally changes gradient scale when valid-target counts change. Match supervised-target counts and sampling frequencies across updates, and report cumulative target exposures; equal epochs or batches alone do not ensure equal supervision. These are proposed experimental controls, not controls verified in the cited studies."}
